speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) in the past three years, of the notifications received to reduce the salary of a Work Permit holder stated in their in-principle approval letter, what proportions are within (i) one month, (ii) one year of the Work Permit issue date; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider a limit on the amount a company is allowed to reduce the salary of the Work Permit holder.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just check further whether 2% is about 14,000 workers every year?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I want to check whether MOM obtains this copy of the written consent to show that the worker accepts the salary reduction, or do we only verify that this written consent exists when a dispute occurs, during the dispute resolution stage.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the first question, certainly, I think that all the foreign workers have direct access to MOM if they want to make a complaint.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And the law protects the worker, especially when there is no documentation provided in terms of a written agreement on the change in salary.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I understand that the reply is that five in 10 of these salary reductions occurred within one year from the Work Permit issue date.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But could I also check whether we have data on how many of the salary reductions occurred before the Work Permit issue date, which means that the foreign workers were promised a salary, but when they arrived in Singapore, the salary was immediately reduced?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Does this conduct constitute providing false information to MOM during the Work Permit application stage?
